matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, calculate the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric discrepancy. This tells you whether the left side must increase, decrease, or stay the same.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the very start of solving, before enumerating any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping the numeric evaluation and moving a stick arbitrarily, which can produce an equation that still does not balance.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Systematically enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved, considering all possible source characters (numerals or operators) and all target positions that could form a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, when generating candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Only considering moves from operators and ignoring potential moves from numerals, thereby missing the correct transformation.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, compute how the move changes the numeric values of the affected numerals and verify that the net change matches the previously computed discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after generating a candidate move, before applying it fully.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that changes a numeral from X to V (decrease of 5) when the discrepancy required an increase of 5, resulting in a false equality.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, check that every resulting symbol (numeral or operator) is a legal Roman numeral or allowed operator; discard any move that leaves a character invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After performing a candidate move, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: Leaving an X with only one diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character repositioning
matchstick.principle: Allow a stick to be moved within the same character, changing its orientation or position to transform the character into another valid numeral (e.g., turning V into X by repositioning a diagonal).
matchstick.when_to_apply: During enumeration of possible transformations, include moves that keep the stick inside its original character.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of repositioning a diagonal within V to form X, thereby missing a valid solution.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of its sticks can turn it into a '-' sign, and the removed stick can be used elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation contains '=', consider using one of its sticks as a source for relocation.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn '=' into a '+' by adding a vertical stick, which is not allowed.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick converts it into a '-' sign, and the removed stick can be placed on another character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+', consider using its vertical stick as a source.
matchstick.example: Removing the horizontal stick from '+' and leaving a lone vertical line, which is not a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick, allow it to be taken from any character (numeral or operator) and placed onto any other character, provided both remain valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the generation of candidate moves, include cross‑character relocations.
matchstick.example: Restricting moves to within the same character, thus missing a solution that requires moving a stick from '=' to '-'.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved directly from one operator to another, simultaneously changing both operators (e.g., moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' to swap them).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains multiple operators, consider moving a stick between them.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '-' to '=', creating an invalid operator like '≠'.

matchstick.title: Source character must stay valid after stick removal
matchstick.principle: Before moving a stick, ensure that the source character can lose that stick and still represent a valid Roman numeral or operator; discard sources such as X, V, L, C, D, M that would become invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During enumeration of possible stick moves, as a filter on source characters.
matchstick.example: Attempting to take a diagonal stick from an X, leaving a single diagonal line (invalid).

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on fixing the numeric balance and forgets that each symbol must remain a legal Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always verify that every character, both source and target, is a valid Roman numeral or allowed operator after the move.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes the move fixes the equation without recomputing the values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recompute the numeric values of both sides after each candidate move and ensure they are equal.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: When relocating a stick, the model may treat the stick as a separate entity and forget to keep the original character placeholder.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain the same number of characters and positions; only relocate sticks, never delete symbols.

matchstick.description: Attempting to change '=' into an invalid operator
matchstick.why_it_happens: Misunderstanding the allowed set of operators and trying to create symbols like '≠' or a single diagonal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only transform '=' into '-' (or '+' if a vertical stick is added) according to the stick rules; never create unsupported symbols.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Focusing on character shapes while forgetting that changing '+' to '-' flips the sign of the operand in the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator changes, recompute the expression using the new operator and verify the numeric equality.
